findings.claim: C209 mutable history semantics despite frozen event types
findings.evidence: CostLedgerEvent and CostLedger are frozen/append-oriented, but attribute_proposal_batch reconstructs every matching historical event with metadata.action_id=node_id and replaces the entire ledger. A later consumption of the same proposal_batch_id therefore overwrites the earlier action attribution without appending a new provider charge or a new attribution event.

findings.claim: two-consumer overwrite is a generic property of every multi-proposal batch
findings.evidence: Cached nodes are pinned to workspace.version and refresh invalidates siblings after a normal state-changing action. Therefore many successful first consumers make same-batch siblings stale. The overwrite remains reachable through no-workspace-change paths: REFINE_ARGUMENT proposal validation checks alignment shape but does not require refined step IDs to exist, while apply_argument returns the unchanged workspace when no refined step/alignment ID hits. A proposal-valid no-op first consumer can therefore leave a sibling from the same batch valid for a second consumption.

findings.claim: C210 canonical reconciliation and branch/obligation accounting semantically require provider metadata.action_id
findings.evidence: CostLedger.reconcile uses event kind/request_id and measurements, structured costing uses AttemptRecord structured_branch_id plus model_usage.structured_branch_id, run_state serializes the ledger generically and builds cost summaries from separate state, and trace_store validates/serializes the ledger generically. tests/test_cost_ledger.py also reconciles shared-batch usage without action_id.

findings.claim: no tracked compatibility dependency on metadata.action_id exists
findings.evidence: tests/test_structured_controller.py contains test_action_runtime_routes_real_generation_to_strong_tier, which explicitly asserts that a provider request metadata.action_id equals the selected action node id. This is a presentation/test compatibility obligation, not evidence canonical cost reconciliation needs the field.

findings.claim: C211 immutable physical events plus append-only consumption edges describes current CSSC behavior
findings.evidence: Current CSSC has no ProposalBatchConsumptionEvent and instead mutates historical metadata through ledger reconstruction. The proposed split is compatible with existing reconciliation in principle because canonical totals do not consult action_id, but that migration itself was not executed or tested in the pinned repository.

findings.claim: C212 current decision trace is sufficient for durable pre-effect replay/OPE
findings.evidence: The in-memory choice_set records node/branch/action, estimated cost, BudgetAdmission and a separate full budget_snapshot; BudgetAdmission may include not_compared dimensions. There is no durable pre-effect ExecutionDecisionEvent, behavior propensity, policy/RNG version, or immutable pre-effect commit. proposal_cache_events are accumulated in _StructuredRunState and serialized only when a ControllerResult is built.

findings.claim: C213-C214 semantic projection and crash tests are verified current behavior
findings.evidence: The pinned source contains neither the proposed journal nor SemanticRunProjectionV0. In particular, the proposed post-migration single-consumer invariant that physical provider events remain byte/field identical after consumption would fail current behavior because action_id is rewritten. Crash-after-decision-before-effect cannot be durably represented by the current result-only trace path.

findings.claim: current action_cost_observed ledger slice exposes proposal-batch consumption attribution mutation
findings.evidence: event_start is captured immediately before execute_action_node; attribute_proposal_batch then rewrites provider events that were emitted before event_start and appends no attribution event. action_cost_observed.ledger_event_ids therefore cannot reveal that causal attribution mutation.

independent_replay.result: Replaying the exact replace-on-matching-batch transformation on a minimal provider request/usage/charge ledger changed metadata.action_id from null to node-A and then to node-B while preserving event ids and measured costs, confirming latest-consumer-wins history semantics independent of cost totals.
independent_replay.scope: This is not a full CSSC runtime or patched migration test.

scope_guards: The caller/test dependency scan is targeted over the pinned authoritative runtime, cost, trace and directly relevant tests; connector code search did not provide a repository-complete grep, so absence elsewhere is not proven.
Two-consumer overwrite is reachable but not generic because state-changing actions invalidate version-pinned sibling proposals.
C211-C214 are architecture/test proposals. Treat their factual premises separately from claims that the migration or journal already exists.
No exploration worker state or feedback was read as downstream judgment input beyond the exact sealed source artifact, and no exploration state/feedback was mutated.
downstream_use: C209 and the targeted C210 dependency result may be used as primary-code-verified evidence with the above reachability and scan-scope guards. C211-C214 should remain proposed migration/journaling/test contracts until implemented and executed at pinned seams.
